page: Amazon Web Services c8ine.xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by dedicated 64-bit x86 Intel processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, the server delivers 4 virtual CPUs distributed across 2 physical CPU cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio (2.0 GB per core). The hardware configuration includes no graphics processing units, centering compute capacity entirely on high-frequency x86 processing tasks.

The instance does not feature bundled local storage, operating without internal solid-state disks and depending entirely on external, network-attached storage architectures for operational and persistent file systems. Network capabilities include a dedicated baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. This architectural configuration optimizes infrastructure spend for compute-focused operations by stripping the overhead of idle local storage arrays, though applications requiring heavy local disk I/O must account for network throughput overhead to remote storage.

Given its compute-heavy profile, high CPU clock rate, and moderate memory density, the c8ine.xlarge is configured for compute-bound workloads that do not demand extensive in-memory state. Primary workload targets include continuous integration and deployment workers, web application hosting, high-throughput distributed microservices, queue processing nodes, and stateless API backend services.
description: Amazon Web Services c8ine.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro System and an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. It delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 2 physical cores, paired with 8.0 GB of memory to maintain a lean 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes onboard graphical accelerators and features no local instance storage, requiring attached network volumes for file operations and persistence. Networking performance includes a baseline allocation of 6 Gbps. By focusing resources strictly on CPU clock frequency and network connectivity rather than massive memory capacities or onboard disks, the c8ine.xlarge provides cost-efficient processing density for CPU-bound tasks. It is well matched for microservices, front-end web serving, continuous integration runners, lightweight compilation jobs, and stateless batch computing workloads.
